description: A quantizer that divides each octave into bands whose widths you set, so a sweep or a random voltage lands on each note as often as its weight says

params.text: Sets how wide a slice of the octave this note takes, 0 to 10; the twelve weights are read against their total, so a weight of zero drops the note entirely

inputs.text: Replaces the knob for that note while a cable is patched, 0 to 10V, and moves the knob to match
The voltage to quantize, one note per polyphonic channel

outputs.text: The quantized voltage, with as many channels as the input

notes: with every weight at zero, which is how a fresh module starts, the input is passed through untouched; turn at least one note up before it quantizes anything
this is not a nearest-note quantizer: each volt's fractional part is cut into bands from C upwards, sized by the weights, so the note follows where in the octave the input lands
